title: Koko Eating Bananas
summary: Find the slowest eating speed that still finishes every pile of bananas within h hours.

tests.explain: At 4 bananas per hour the piles take 1 + 3 + 1 + 2 = 7 hours, one too many. At 5 per hour they take 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 6 hours, which fits.
There are 4 piles and only 4 hours, so each pile must be finished in one hour. The speed must be at least the biggest pile, 25.
At 3 per hour the pile takes 4 hours (3 + 3 + 3 + 1). At 4 per hour it takes 3 hours (4 + 4 + 2).

hints: For a fixed speed k, how many hours does it take? Each pile p needs Math.ceil(p / k) hours, because a started hour is a whole hour.
If speed k is fast enough, every speed above k is too. Feasibility flips from false to true exactly once, so you can binary search over the speed itself.
Search k in [1, max(piles)]. If hoursAt(mid) <= h, mid works and so might something slower: hi = mid. Otherwise lo = mid + 1. Return lo.

complexity.time: O(n log m): log m candidate speeds, where m is the largest pile, each checked in O(n)
